Class RenderClock

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tui.RenderClock
public final class RenderClock extends Object
Measures the real time between renders, so animations advance by actual elapsed time rather than by a fixed per-tick amount.

This mirrors the model used by the ratatui effects library (tachyonfx), where the host measures the time since the last draw and advances effects by it. Measuring at the render means an input-driven redraw between two ticks advances an animation only by the little time that really passed, so the animation does not speed up while keys are pressed or the mouse moves.

Times are read from System.nanoTime(), which only moves forward, so setting the system clock does not affect animations and the elapsed time is never negative. The time below a millisecond is carried to the next render, so there is no truncation drift. A gap longer than 250L ms, such as a laptop sleep or a debugger pause, is clamped, so an animation does not jump far ahead after it.

Not thread-safe: a runner uses it from its render thread only.

  • Method Details

    • tick

      public Duration tick()
      Returns the real time since the previous call, as whole milliseconds with the remainder carried to the next call. The first call after creation or reset() returns zero. The result is never negative and never more than 250L ms.
      Returns:
      the time to advance animations by for this render

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Forgets the timing, so the next tick() returns zero and starts a fresh animation. A runner calls this while nothing is animating, so an animation that starts later does not pick up the idle time before it.
